title: Scraper controller playbook
description: The only executable guard between a malformed legal letter and a send path. Every constraint here exists because tools/spec-audit/negative.mjs proved its absence let something unsendable through. Invariants that JSON Schema cannot express (cross-field disjointness, template-variable binding, version monotonicity) live in tools/spec-audit/playbook-lint.mjs and are enforced by the same CI job — see that file before assuming an omission here is a hole.

kind.description: RIGHTS_REQUEST = a statutory instrument with an Art. 12(3) clock and an Art. 77 route. ENROLMENT = a non-statutory suppression enrolment or fraud marker: no clock, no escalation. Required (not defaulted) because JSON Schema defaults are annotation-only and are never applied by a validator.

active.description: Required. A shipped playbook is active:false until counsel signs off against this version. Do not rely on a schema default here — validators do not apply defaults, so an omitted flag would read as unset, not false.

parameterised.description: True only for generic templates carrying __PARAM__ placeholders (e.g. loeschung.generic-adresshaendler). Placeholder-bearing values are rejected outright unless this is true, and a parameterised playbook may never be active:true. Clone it and fill the placeholders to make it sendable.

registered.description: Per-channel Einwurf-Einschreiben. Postal-only: registered email is not a thing. A registered send is the ONLY thing that starts the Art. 12(3) clock (CLAUDE.md §6).

seatDpa.description: Competent supervisory authority for an Art. 77 complaint. Closed enum: a free-text typo silently misroutes a complaint to an authority with no jurisdiction, and the user never learns why nothing happened.

venue.description: The escalation venue when there is no German SEAT to name — i.e. the alternative to seatDpa, not a supplement to it. USER_RESIDENCE = the competent authority follows the DATA SUBJECT's habitual residence (Art. 77(1)), which is the venue for a controller with no German establishment: a US/UK enrichment broker has no seat DPA, so its Art. 77 complaint is lodged at the Land DPA of the user who is complaining, and that is only knowable at escalation time. ONE VALUE, DELIBERATELY. This is not a stub for a venue taxonomy and must not grow into one — every other venue in this product is a fixed German seat and is expressed by seatDpa's closed enum. USER_RESIDENCE exists solely because that enum cannot say "dynamic, resolved from the user", and before this field a playbook that omitted seatDpa was ambiguous between "dynamic by design" and "someone forgot" (the second happened: 13 of 19 shipped playbooks could reach ESCALATION_DRAFTED with no venue recorded anywhere). Declaring it makes the omission a statement instead of a silence. TODO(counsel): venue values are counsel-owned per controller; this field only makes them expressible.

enrolment.description: Only on kind: ENROLMENT. The non-statutory counterpart of deadlineDays+escalation.

scopeSource.description: Where the letter's bounded SCOPE comes from, when it is not derivable from the identity. PROVENANCE_ANSWER = the category list and source names of an Art. 17(1)(d) partial erasure, taken from this same controller's own prior Art. 15(1)(g) answer. Declaring it makes the engine REFUSE to render without a PartialErasureScope; omitting it on a template that lists categories renders the list as nothing, which turns a bounded demand into an unbounded erasure demand at a bureau — silently, because {{#each}} over an unsupplied list is empty rather than an error. Closed enum: any other provenance for a scope is a new legal instrument, not a config value.

accepts.description: The CEILING of what we will hand over, minimised. Not a wish list.

then.description: required:true with accepts:[none] demands proof the playbook refuses to supply — the request is unsendable by construction.

subjectFields.description: WHICH verified-identity fields the template needs. Closed enum by design: this is not, and must never become, a place to express WHOSE data to request. See CLAUDE.md, the rule that outranks all others.

deadlineDays.description: Art. 12(3) is one month (28 = shortest month). Up to 90 covers the Art. 12(3) two-month extension. A short deadline is not a shortcut: asserting a 1-day clock to a controller is legally meaningless and reads as bad faith.

humanReviewIfConfidenceBelow.description: REQUIRED. This is the docs/06 C4 anti-prompt-injection control: below it, parser output may not decide COMPLIED/REFUSED/INCOMPLETE and the only allowed target is NEEDS_HUMAN. It was previously omissible AND settable to 0, either of which lets a hostile broker letter auto-decide its own outcome. Floor of 0.5 because below half confidence the parser is worse than a coin flip.

escalation.description: An empty escalation object used to be valid, which meant silent no-escalation on a playbook that looked escalatable. Both outcomes must be stated explicitly, including when the answer is NONE.

allOf.$comment: kind: RIGHTS_REQUEST — statutory, so it carries a clock and an escalation route.

kind: ENROLMENT — non-statutory, so declaring a deadline or an Art. 77 route is a category error. That covers BOTH ways of naming an Art. 77 venue — seatDpa and venue are each forbidden here — because a suppression enrolment has no supervisory complaint to route. Note this branch is never reached by the C2 conditional below (it requires an escalation, which an ENROLMENT may not have); these two lines are what stops a venue being declared on an enrolment anyway.
The primary channel must have somewhere to send to.
...and so must the fallback, or the fallback is a lie.
C1: a playbook that escalates on SILENCE must be able to reach a provable send, or deadlineAt is never set and the silence path dead-ends. Requires postal+registered on the primary or the fallback.

C2 (decision D4): a playbook that can draft an Art. 77 complaint must say WHERE it gets filed. Until this existed, seatDpa was schema-required on exactly one shape (ACCESS_ART15_SOURCE, below), nothing read it at escalation time, and the venue for a controller with no German seat — the user's own Land DPA — could not be written down at all. So an absent seatDpa was ambiguous between 'dynamic by design' and 'someone forgot', and 13 of 19 shipped playbooks reached ESCALATION_DRAFTED with no venue recorded anywhere; the missing seatDpa on explanation.retorio (whose own header says to set BAYLDA before activation) is the proof that forgetting happens. Either answer is acceptable, silence is not. NOTE ON SHAPE: `escalation` is an OBJECT with three named triggers, not a list, so this cannot use `contains` — 'any trigger is DRAFT_ART77' has to be an anyOf over the three properties. Each branch carries its own `required` because `properties` alone is vacuously satisfied by an ABSENT property, and onIncompleteSourceList is optional: without the `required` guard the third branch would match every playbook that simply omits it, and the conditional would fire everywhere instead of where it means something.
The flagship extracts nothing without a provenance block; onIncompleteSourceList is meaningless without one.

scopeSource: PROVENANCE_ANSWER is the Art. 17(1)(d) partial-erasure chain and nothing else. On an access or objection playbook it would mean a letter whose scope is bounded by facts the instrument never establishes.
onIncompleteSourceList only has meaning for a source request.
docs/07: a full ID copy to action a bare Art. 21(2) marketing objection is over-collection. The template pushes back on the demand; it does not satisfy it.
Unresolved __PARAM__ placeholders are rejected unless the playbook is explicitly parameterised.
A parameterised playbook is a stencil, never a sendable artefact.

templateName.$comment: Also blocks path traversal: '../../etc/passwd' cannot match.

emailAddress.$comment: Both format and pattern on purpose: `format` is annotation-only unless the consumer registers ajv-formats, so the pattern is the constraint that actually bites.

matcher.$comment: The real grammar every shipped playbook already uses. This was `{"type": "object"}` — entirely unconstrained — so the matcher syntax the engine depends on was the one thing the schema never validated.

needleList.$comment: minLength 3: a one- or two-character needle matches almost any German letter and would auto-decide outcomes on noise.

condition.$comment: Exactly one of anyOf / allOf / responseContains. An empty condition matched nothing while looking like a rule.
